answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a costly, verifiable signal before joining a market: the kernel of the design is a refundable bond locked per identity, slashed when peers detect duplicate behaviour. Honest agents earn the bond back through useful work, while an attacker must fund a separate bond for every fake island of identities, so the cost of forging a thousand agents scales linearly with the stake and quickly exceeds any profit from manipulating reputation or rewards.
